sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
UChicago bachelor’s completed by matriculation is eligible in degree type; academic eligibility additionally
requires 3.0 in junior/senior and post-baccalaureate work, 3.5 upper-division math GPA, and at least 12
quarter/8 semester substantial upper-division math courses. Exceptions only for demonstrated exceptional
quantitative ability. International applicants need comparable record. PhD admission only; MA/MAT suspended.
[s1] [s2]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Select pure or applied area and field in application; choose only one UCLA major. Prepare transcripts, required
math-course list, SOP, personal statement, three letters, Math GRE and fee/waiver evidence. Check whether
department still wants original transcripts at application. [s1] [s2] [s5]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Select research field; SOP may identify mentors. No supervisor agreement listed as a precondition. Reach out
only with specific fit questions and confirm 2027 capacity. [s2] [s5]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Use UCLA graduate application; one major. Send referee invitations after entry, track receipt and reminders;
submit on time despite pending letters. Updates go directly to department. Public research did not create an
application. [s4] [s5] [s7]
Cycle verification [Conflict]
2027-28 program gives 13 December 2026. Several department instructions retain obsolete English tests,
physical-mail language and inconsistent funding/grace-period rules. [s1] [s2] [s6]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
TOEFL 87 before 21 January 2026 or 4.5 on/after that date; IELTS Academic 7.0. No TOEFL MyBest. Scores valid
two years at application; latest test only. Admission proficiency, academic writing placement and TA oral
proficiency are distinct requirements. [s6]
UChicago English exemption [Conflict]
Completed or forthcoming accredited US bachelor’s degree qualifies for admission-test exemption. UChicago
undergraduate degree also meets central prior-education route for TA oral-proficiency eligibility. Department
blanket TOP requirement for non-native speakers conflicts with this newer central exemption: verify application
to math funding. [s6] [s2]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Not listed among required tests; current math program specifies only Subject Mathematics. Public source does
not establish whether unsolicited General GRE is considered or ignored; not required should not be read as
forbidden. [s1] [s2]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Standing rule]
No exact annual mathematics stipend published on reviewed admissions, financial-support or handbook pages;
amounts vary annually. Guarantee normally includes living income, full registration fees, health insurance and
nonresident tuition. Obtain 2027-28 gross cash, appointment months and summer amount from offer.
Cost-of-attendance or maximum-support limits are not stipend offers. Published UC contract Table B.1 provides
UCLA Group 2, salary point 1, 50% TA appointment USD 4,323/month effective October 1, 2026 and USD
4,432/month effective October 1, 2027. These are contractual monthly appointment rates, not a promised
12-month Mathematics package; multiply only by actual paid months in the offer. [s2] [s3] [s10] [ucwages27]
Years of support [Conflict]
Dedicated support page: almost all admits guaranteed five years. International admissions subsection: four
years guaranteed, fifth usually if good standing and advanced to candidacy. Official conflict; individual offer
must specify duration. [s2] [s3]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International students eligible for departmental fellowships/TA/RA and nonresident tuition support. US
federal/need-based loans and work-study generally unavailable. Some extramural/RTG awards have separate
citizenship restrictions. [s2] [s3] [s9]
Conditions and duties [Conflict]
Support mixes fellowships/TA/RA, good progress and sometimes advancement to candidacy. Department says
TOP pass within first year for non-native speakers; central rule exempts qualifying US-undergraduate degree
holders. Clarify summer and fifth-year guarantee. [s2] [s3] [s6]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
Automatic ordinary mathematics support. Central merit-award application is embedded in graduate
application; continuing awards may need yearly reapplication. [s3] [s8]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Government/home-country or international awards pursued separately; GRAPES database lists extramural
opportunities. Readerships require 3.2 GPA and two college-calculus years. Named NSF/Hertz/Ford examples
on older departmental page are not evidence of this applicant’s eligibility or current availability. [s2] [s3]
Application fee [Standing rule]
US $155 for international applicants, nonrefundable, credit/debit card. [s5]

Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Request in Fee Waiver section with proof before submission/payment. Enrolled noncitizen/nonresident
need-based route requires California-state need aid, so ordinary UChicago aid does not satisfy that route.
Listed research-program participation or eligible in-person recruitment-event route may apply; verify individual
participation and current-cycle event code. Public event text still labels 2026-27. [s4] [s5]

Pay attention to
• Math GRE required; course-list upload required; no publications for international applicants.
• Exact support duration and English/TOP policy conflict across official pages.
• No confirmed math annual stipend amount; do not confuse financial-aid budget with cash funding.
• Gieseker, Mark Green and Hida are not treated as ordinary active advisers without current appointment
checks. Faculty-paper coverage is incomplete for Blasius and Robert Greene; complex-analysis research such
as Bonk is adjacent rather than complex algebraic geometry.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
UChicago bachelor’s completed by matriculation is eligible in degree type; academic eligibility additionally
requires 3.0 in junior/senior and post-baccalaureate work, 3.5 upper-division math GPA, and at least 12
quarter/8 semester substantial upper-division math courses. Exceptions only for demonstrated exceptional
quantitative ability. International applicants need comparable record. PhD admission only; MA/MAT suspended.
[s1] [s2]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Select pure or applied area and field in application; choose only one UCLA major. Prepare transcripts, required
math-course list, SOP, personal statement, three letters, Math GRE and fee/waiver evidence. Check whether
department still wants original transcripts at application. [s1] [s2] [s5]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Select research field; SOP may identify mentors. No supervisor agreement listed as a precondition. Reach out
only with specific fit questions and confirm 2027 capacity. [s2] [s5]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Use UCLA graduate application; one major. Send referee invitations after entry, track receipt and reminders;
submit on time despite pending letters. Updates go directly to department. Public research did not create an
application. [s4] [s5] [s7]
Cycle verification [Conflict]
2027-28 program gives 13 December 2026. Several department instructions retain obsolete English tests,
physical-mail language and inconsistent funding/grace-period rules. [s1] [s2] [s6]
Deadlines by stage
Academic application [2027 confirmed]
13 December 2026. Time and time zone not established on math listing or department page; verify portal
cutoff. [s1]
Funding consideration [Standing rule]
Ordinary math support automatic with admission; use 13 December 2026. Central funding FAQ says December
15 for entering support with departmental exceptions; separate merit-award fields are within admission
application. Do not assume two extra days for math. [s1] [s3] [s8] [s9]

undated grace policy, not an exact 2027 calendar date. [s2]

January and elsewhere all materials through end of second week. Exact 2027 grace cutoff unconfirmed. GRE
code 4837, math 0703; central advice test by November. [s2] [s7]

requirement. [s1] [s2] [s7]

English and GRE
English requirement [Standing rule]
TOEFL 87 before 21 January 2026 or 4.5 on/after that date; IELTS Academic 7.0. No TOEFL MyBest. Scores valid
two years at application; latest test only. Admission proficiency, academic writing placement and TA oral
proficiency are distinct requirements. [s6]
UChicago English exemption [Conflict]
Completed or forthcoming accredited US bachelor’s degree qualifies for admission-test exemption. UChicago
undergraduate degree also meets central prior-education route for TA oral-proficiency eligibility. Department
blanket TOP requirement for non-native speakers conflicts with this newer central exemption: verify application
to math funding. [s6] [s2]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Not listed among required tests; current math program specifies only Subject Mathematics. Public source does
not establish whether unsolicited General GRE is considered or ignored; not required should not be read as
forbidden. [s1] [s2]
GRE Mathematics [2027 confirmed]
Required in current 2027-28 program listing and department checklist. No public 2027 exception identified. [s1]
[s2]
Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Conflict]
Upload actual unofficial transcript (not grade audit/progress report), with institution/student/program/major,
term courses, units, grades and grading legend. Department additionally says scans and originals, mailed
sealed official records; central rules permit departmental original-at-application requirements. Ask whether this
legacy instruction remains operative. [s2] [s7]
Mathematics-course list [Standing rule]
Required list of mathematics courses taken. Department publishes no template, page/word limit, whether
textbooks or planned courses must be listed, or precise upload format; inspect math supplement before
preparing final list. [s2]

Three, preferably all and at least two from mathematicians familiar with recent work; additional letters not
considered helpful by departmental FAQ. [s1] [s2]

Ordinary math support automatic, with no separate reference identified. Central merit-award portal may

After entering names/emails, applicant can send invitations. This is a send action, not evidence that merely
typing a name immediately invites. [s4]

Letters may arrive after applicant submits; invitations/reminders available through application and not

Letters of Recommendation section shows submitted status; applicant can resend notification/reminders.

Required upload. Central prompt paraphrase: purpose/subfields, preparation and research outcomes, other
relevant experience, UCLA fit/potential mentors, career plans. Central page says programs choose
500/1,000/1,500-word caps; math cap and typography not publicly established. Verify before drafting to
length. [s2] [s5]
Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
Central application requests personal statement, maximum 500 words, approximately one single-spaced page,
1-inch margins, 12-point font. Prompt paraphrase: choose one or more: formative personal/educational
circumstances; obstacles and persistence; leadership/service benefiting others; alignment with UCLA
community principles. Used for some merit awards. [s5]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
Indicate area/field in application and research interests/potential mentors within SOP. Separate essay not
identified. [s2] [s5]

Department explicitly instructs international applicants not to send publications. No standalone thesis/writing
sample requirement or permission found; ask before uploading a paper. [s2]

Amount and coverage [Standing rule]
No exact annual mathematics stipend published on reviewed admissions, financial-support or handbook pages;
amounts vary annually. Guarantee normally includes living income, full registration fees, health insurance and
nonresident tuition. Obtain 2027-28 gross cash, appointment months and summer amount from offer.
Cost-of-attendance or maximum-support limits are not stipend offers. Published UC contract Table B.1 provides
UCLA Group 2, salary point 1, 50% TA appointment USD 4,323/month effective October 1, 2026 and USD
4,432/month effective October 1, 2027. These are contractual monthly appointment rates, not a promised
12-month Mathematics package; multiply only by actual paid months in the offer. [s2] [s3] [s10] [ucwages27]
Years of support [Conflict]
Dedicated support page: almost all admits guaranteed five years. International admissions subsection: four
years guaranteed, fifth usually if good standing and advanced to candidacy. Official conflict; individual offer
must specify duration. [s2] [s3]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International students eligible for departmental fellowships/TA/RA and nonresident tuition support. US
federal/need-based loans and work-study generally unavailable. Some extramural/RTG awards have separate
citizenship restrictions. [s2] [s3] [s9]
Conditions and duties [Conflict]
Support mixes fellowships/TA/RA, good progress and sometimes advancement to candidacy. Department says
TOP pass within first year for non-native speakers; central rule exempts qualifying US-undergraduate degree
holders. Clarify summer and fifth-year guarantee. [s2] [s3] [s6]

Automatic ordinary mathematics support. Central merit-award application is embedded in graduate
application; continuing awards may need yearly reapplication. [s3] [s8]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Government/home-country or international awards pursued separately; GRAPES database lists extramural
opportunities. Readerships require 3.2 GPA and two college-calculus years. Named NSF/Hertz/Ford examples
on older departmental page are not evidence of this applicant’s eligibility or current availability. [s2] [s3]

US $155 for international applicants, nonrefundable, credit/debit card. [s5]

Pay attention to
• Math GRE required; course-list upload required; no publications for international applicants.
• Exact support duration and English/TOP policy conflict across official pages.
• No confirmed math annual stipend amount; do not confuse financial-aid budget with cash funding.
• Gieseker, Mark Green and Hida are not treated as ordinary active advisers without current appointment
checks. Faculty-paper coverage is incomplete for Blasius and Robert Greene; complex-analysis research such
as Bonk is adjacent rather than complex algebraic geometry.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
UChicago bachelor’s completed by matriculation is eligible in degree type; academic eligibility additionally
requires 3.0 in junior/senior and post-baccalaureate work, 3.5 upper-division math GPA, and at least 12
quarter/8 semester substantial upper-division math courses. Exceptions only for demonstrated exceptional
quantitative ability. International applicants need comparable record. PhD admission only; MA/MAT suspended.
[s1] [s2]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Select pure or applied area and field in application; choose only one UCLA major. Prepare transcripts, required
math-course list, SOP, personal statement, three letters, Math GRE and fee/waiver evidence. Check whether
department still wants original transcripts at application. [s1] [s2] [s5]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Select research field; SOP may identify mentors. No supervisor agreement listed as a precondition. Reach out
only with specific fit questions and confirm 2027 capacity. [s2] [s5]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Use UCLA graduate application; one major. Send referee invitations after entry, track receipt and reminders;
submit on time despite pending letters. Updates go directly to department. Public research did not create an
application. [s4] [s5] [s7]
Cycle verification [Conflict]
2027-28 program gives 13 December 2026. Several department instructions retain obsolete English tests,
physical-mail language and inconsistent funding/grace-period rules. [s1] [s2] [s6]
Deadlines by stage
Academic application [2027 confirmed]
13 December 2026. Time and time zone not established on math listing or department page; verify portal
cutoff. [s1]
Funding consideration [Standing rule]
Ordinary math support automatic with admission; use 13 December 2026. Central funding FAQ says December
15 for entering support with departmental exceptions; separate merit-award fields are within admission
application. Do not assume two extra days for math. [s1] [s3] [s8] [s9]

Reference receipt [Conflict]
Aim for 13 December 2026. Department says review begins late December and all materials needed then; its
FAQ permits late letters/materials but says incomplete if absent by end of second week in January. This is an
undated grace policy, not an exact 2027 calendar date. [s2]
Test-score receipt [Conflict]
Aim for application deadline; department inconsistently says scores accepted through end of first week in
January and elsewhere all materials through end of second week. Exact 2027 grace cutoff unconfirmed. GRE
code 4837, math 0703; central advice test by November. [s2] [s7]
Supporting documents [Conflict]
Upload applicant-controlled materials by 13 December 2026. Department’s late-material passages use late
December/end of second January week, with no exact current date. Confirm original transcript delivery
requirement. [s1] [s2] [s7]
Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
Exact mathematics 2027 offer-acceptance date not established. Central award page links CGS resolution, but
this alone does not verify a current signatory/individual offer deadline. [s8]
English and GRE
English requirement [Standing rule]
TOEFL 87 before 21 January 2026 or 4.5 on/after that date; IELTS Academic 7.0. No TOEFL MyBest. Scores valid
two years at application; latest test only. Admission proficiency, academic writing placement and TA oral
proficiency are distinct requirements. [s6]
UChicago English exemption [Conflict]
Completed or forthcoming accredited US bachelor’s degree qualifies for admission-test exemption. UChicago
undergraduate degree also meets central prior-education route for TA oral-proficiency eligibility. Department
blanket TOP requirement for non-native speakers conflicts with this newer central exemption: verify application
to math funding. [s6] [s2]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Not listed among required tests; current math program specifies only Subject Mathematics. Public source does
not establish whether unsolicited General GRE is considered or ignored; not required should not be read as
forbidden. [s1] [s2]
GRE Mathematics [2027 confirmed]
Required in current 2027-28 program listing and department checklist. No public 2027 exception identified. [s1]
[s2]
Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Conflict]
Upload actual unofficial transcript (not grade audit/progress report), with institution/student/program/major,
term courses, units, grades and grading legend. Department additionally says scans and originals, mailed
sealed official records; central rules permit departmental original-at-application requirements. Ask whether this
legacy instruction remains operative. [s2] [s7]
Mathematics-course list [Standing rule]
Required list of mathematics courses taken. Department publishes no template, page/word limit, whether
textbooks or planned courses must be listed, or precise upload format; inspect math supplement before
preparing final list. [s2]

Course descriptions [Unresolved]
Department lists illustrative UCLA prerequisite course descriptions; this does not itself require applicant syllabi.
Applicant-specific descriptions/textbook fields unverified in public instructions. [s2]
Recommendation letters
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three, preferably all and at least two from mathematicians familiar with recent work; additional letters not
considered helpful by departmental FAQ. [s1] [s2]
Scholarship references [Unresolved]
Ordinary math support automatic, with no separate reference identified. Central merit-award portal may
request award-specific data; exact extra-reference forms not public in reviewed pages. [s3] [s8]
What sends the invitation [Standing rule]
After entering names/emails, applicant can send invitations. This is a send action, not evidence that merely
typing a name immediately invites. [s4]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
Letters may arrive after applicant submits; invitations/reminders available through application and not
restricted to after final submission. [s4]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
Letters of Recommendation section shows submitted status; applicant can resend notification/reminders.
Application-material inquiries otherwise go to department. [s4]
Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
Updates generally sent directly to program. Public graduate FAQ does not establish letter-content replacement
or prior-cycle reuse; academic-job RECRUIT reuse instructions do not apply to graduate admission. [s4] [s7]
Written materials
Academic CV / resume [Unresolved]
Not listed on public math checklist; required/optional portal status, limit and upload rules unverified. [s1] [s2]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
Required upload. Central prompt paraphrase: purpose/subfields, preparation and research outcomes, other
relevant experience, UCLA fit/potential mentors, career plans. Central page says programs choose
500/1,000/1,500-word caps; math cap and typography not publicly established. Verify before drafting to
length. [s2] [s5]
Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
Central application requests personal statement, maximum 500 words, approximately one single-spaced page,
1-inch margins, 12-point font. Prompt paraphrase: choose one or more: formative personal/educational
circumstances; obstacles and persistence; leadership/service benefiting others; alignment with UCLA
community principles. Used for some merit awards. [s5]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
Indicate area/field in application and research interests/potential mentors within SOP. Separate essay not
identified. [s2] [s5]
Research proposal [Unresolved]
No standalone research proposal listed; separate prompt, limit and upload permission unverified. [s1] [s2]
Writing sample / thesis / research summary [Standing rule]
Department explicitly instructs international applicants not to send publications. No standalone thesis/writing
sample requirement or permission found; ask before uploading a paper. [s2]

Publications list [Standing rule]
Do not send publications, per international-applicant department instructions. Separate bibliographic list/CV
slot rules unverified. [s2]
Course-list document [Standing rule]
Required list of mathematics courses taken. Department publishes no template, page/word limit, whether
textbooks or planned courses must be listed, or precise upload format; inspect math supplement before
preparing final list. [s2]
Scholarship essays [Standing rule]
Ordinary departmental support requires no separate application. Central merit awards use admission-portal
funding fields and personal statement; public pages do not expose all award-specific prompts/limits. Do not
infer eligibility for citizenship-restricted awards. [s3] [s5] [s8] [s15]
Other short answers / materials [Unresolved]
No other math-specific essay publicly listed. Current portal may contain additional short answers or funding
fields; exact prompts unverified. [s2] [s5]
Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [Standing rule]
No exact annual mathematics stipend published on reviewed admissions, financial-support or handbook pages;
amounts vary annually. Guarantee normally includes living income, full registration fees, health insurance and
nonresident tuition. Obtain 2027-28 gross cash, appointment months and summer amount from offer.
Cost-of-attendance or maximum-support limits are not stipend offers. Published UC contract Table B.1 provides
UCLA Group 2, salary point 1, 50% TA appointment USD 4,323/month effective October 1, 2026 and USD
4,432/month effective October 1, 2027. These are contractual monthly appointment rates, not a promised
12-month Mathematics package; multiply only by actual paid months in the offer. [s2] [s3] [s10] [ucwages27]
Years of support [Conflict]
Dedicated support page: almost all admits guaranteed five years. International admissions subsection: four
years guaranteed, fifth usually if good standing and advanced to candidacy. Official conflict; individual offer
must specify duration. [s2] [s3]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International students eligible for departmental fellowships/TA/RA and nonresident tuition support. US
federal/need-based loans and work-study generally unavailable. Some extramural/RTG awards have separate
citizenship restrictions. [s2] [s3] [s9]
Conditions and duties [Conflict]
Support mixes fellowships/TA/RA, good progress and sometimes advancement to candidacy. Department says
TOP pass within first year for non-native speakers; central rule exempts qualifying US-undergraduate degree
holders. Clarify summer and fifth-year guarantee. [s2] [s3] [s6]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
Automatic ordinary mathematics support. Central merit-award application is embedded in graduate
application; continuing awards may need yearly reapplication. [s3] [s8]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Government/home-country or international awards pursued separately; GRAPES database lists extramural
opportunities. Readerships require 3.2 GPA and two college-calculus years. Named NSF/Hertz/Ford examples
on older departmental page are not evidence of this applicant’s eligibility or current availability. [s2] [s3]
Application fee [Standing rule]
US $155 for international applicants, nonrefundable, credit/debit card. [s5]

Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Request in Fee Waiver section with proof before submission/payment. Enrolled noncitizen/nonresident
need-based route requires California-state need aid, so ordinary UChicago aid does not satisfy that route.
Listed research-program participation or eligible in-person recruitment-event route may apply; verify individual
participation and current-cycle event code. Public event text still labels 2026-27. [s4] [s5]
Conflicts and remaining checks
Conflicting sources [Conflict]
Four versus five years guaranteed; blanket TOP testing versus US-degree exemption; first versus second
January week score grace; original-transcript requirement needs confirmation; current personal statement
appears centrally but not department checklist. [s2] [s3] [s5] [s6] [s7]
Checks still needed [Unresolved]
Confirm cutoff time/timezone; exact late-material cutoff; original transcript requirement; SOP math
cap/course-list fields; CV/extra-document permissions; referee replacement/reuse; award-specific forms; 2027
stipend and summer/fifth-year coverage; degree-based TOP exemption; offer response date. [s1] [s2] [s4] [s5] [s6]
